name: Daniel J. Crothers
description: Concurred, argued that N.D.C.C. ch. 12.1-19.1 is unconstitutionally vague, particularly its health-risk exception, and the vague parts cannot be severed, thus the entire law should be invalidated.

name: Jerod E. Tufte
description: Dissented, argued that the majority opinion extends the vagueness standard to natural rights and permits pre-enforcement facial challenges based on hypotheticals, concluding the law is not unconstitutionally vague and does not conflict with Article I, Section 1.

name: Douglas A. Bahr
description: Concurred, argued that H.B. 1340 is a valid exercise of the legislature's constitutional authority to create political subdivisions and define the powers of home rule cities, and that it preempts Fargo's ordinances.

name: Crothers, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that S.B. 2015 violated the single subject rule of the North Dakota Constitution, rendering the entire bill void.

name: Jensen, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that while the legislation violated the single subject rule, the underlying action would have been permissible, and the judgment should be stayed for 30 days to allow the legislature to re-enact the legislation constitutionally.

name: McEvers, Justice
description: Concurred, agreed that the legislation violated the single subject rule and that the judgment should be stayed for 30 days, but did not speculate on the likelihood of the legislation surviving further consideration.

name: Gary H. Lee, D.J.
description: Concurred with Justice McEvers' special concurrence.

name: Jerod E. Tufte
description: Concurred, argued that the district court did not commit reversible error regarding public trial, double jeopardy, jury instructions, or the admission of the victim's video.

name: Lisa Fair McEvers
description: Concurred, arguing that the common law doctrine of abatement ab initio is inconsistent with North Dakota's constitutional victims' rights, and since there are no collateral consequences or requests for substitution, the appeal is moot and the judgment stands.

name: JENSEN, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the North Dakota Constitution guarantees a fundamental right to abortion to preserve a woman's life or health, and the challenged statute is not narrowly tailored.

name: Tufte, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the "life or health" right need not be understood more broadly than self-defense, and the statute is unconstitutional for not providing an exception for life-saving abortions.

name: McEvers, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the North Dakota Constitution's protected rights may be broader than those under the United States Constitution, and the court upheld the injunction on narrow grounds.

name: Justice Gerald W.VandeWalle
description: Other, argued that he was not a member of the Court when the opinion was considered and did not participate.

name: Jerod E. Tufte
description: Concurred, argued that the Secretary of State misapplied the law by invalidating all signatures notarized by a single notary based on an imputed pattern of fraud, rather than only those demonstrably fraudulent.

name: Jon J. Jensen
description: Concurred, argued that quick-take procedures were available for the sewer project and the district court did not abuse its discretion in excluding evidence based on an incorrect interpretation of zoning ordinances.

name: Gerald W. VandeWalle
description: Concurred, arguing that the North Dakota Constitution preserves the right to a jury trial for municipal ordinance violations that carried potential penalties of imprisonment or significant fines at the time of its adoption, even if the offense is now categorized as an infraction.
